verdict_reason: 34 photos from 7 photographers were on disk and essentially all of the identifiable ones show one place: Den Ngoc Son and its approach across Cau The Huc on Hoan Kiem Lake. Independent hard proofs from three different photographers: the Nghi Mon entrance pillars bearing the giant red characters PHUC/LOC and 山仰止, the Dac Nguyet Lau gate with its 得月樓 plaque, the Long Mon gate with the 硯臺筆塔大塊文章 inscription and dragon/tiger reliefs, the red The Huc bridge, the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion with the lake behind it, and a trilingual interpretive board reading 'DEN NGOC SON / NGOC'SON TEMPLE / TEMPLE DE LA MONTAGNE DE JADE'. The pin therefore sits on the real subject, not on a place centroid. Only a handful of context-free close-ups (a selfie, a ceramic lion, incense-stick and banyan-root macros) cannot be tied to it.
place_if_genuine: Ngoc Son Temple, Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi

photos.evidence: Green-brown lake water with willows on the far bank, a low stone lakeside terrace with blue-and-white ceramic planters holding bonsai on stone tables, and a small timber jetty - the bonsai terrace on the Hoan Kiem lakeshore/Ngoc Son island.

Bronze incense burner with dragon handles standing in front of tall red-lacquered plank doors. No text. Same photographer and consecutive upload id as 2803345142 (Hoan Kiem lakeshore), and the red doors match the Ngoc Son halls.

Dark Vietnamese temple altar: gilded carved shrine frame, gladioli and lotus, brass candlesticks, a yellow ceremonial parasol overhead, red-lacquered altar table. Nothing legible and no exterior context.
Macro of a curtain of brown and yellow banyan aerial roots against a trunk. No built context at all.

The Nghi Mon entrance gate: two grey rendered pillars with dragon panels on top, white panels bearing huge red characters 祿 (Loc) and 福 (Phuc), and the couplets 山仰止 / 王泮斯 - the unique outer gate of Ngoc Son on Dinh Tien Hoang.

photos.place: The Huc Bridge, Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Vermilion-red timber bridge on red piles with lattice balustrades curving across green lake water, people on the deck - Cau The Huc to Ngoc Son island.
The Dac Nguyet Lau gate: two-tier tiled roof, blue-ground panel with two gold dragons flanking a circular moon opening, and the legible plaque 得月樓.

Grey rendered wall, red-lacquered panelled door, white vertical scroll couplets in Han characters (金門鐘响... / 白水波...), pantiled roof with a red fascia board. Same wall fabric, roof and couplet boards as the confirmed Ngoc Son halls, and it sits inside the same continuous upload run 4316-4318.

Red-lacquered temple facade with red silk lanterns, a bronze incense urn on a stone plinth in a paved courtyard, frangipani branches overhead, winter-dressed Vietnamese worshippers. Same courtyard as 4317080808/4317962337; inside the confirmed Ngoc Son upload run.

Woman raising a bundle of burning incense over a stone/bronze urn in front of red-lacquered columns and doors; smoke-filled red interior. Same courtyard furniture and upload run as the confirmed Ngoc Son shots.

The Dac Nguyet Lau gate again, seen head-on: tiled double roof, blue panel with two gold dragons around a circular moon opening, flanking couplet boards and a glazed dragon relief on the right wall; red bridge railing bottom-right.

Souvenir stall (conical hats, straw hats, brass gongs, glass display cases) under a red-pillared, pantile-roofed temple building with red-ground vertical banners in gold Han characters. Matches the Ngoc Son side buildings and lies inside the confirmed 4316-4318 run.

Roof detail: white plaster flaming-disc finial on the ridge, a green glazed ceramic phoenix at each ridge end, pierced openwork frieze panels under the eaves, two courses of old red pantiles. Same building fabric as 4317963013 and the confirmed Ngoc Son halls.

Red-lacquered hall front with red lanterns, large bronze urn on a stone base, four women praying with incense, and a grey stone pillar with a vertical Han inscription at right. Same courtyard as 4316346061.

Paved temple courtyard: open pavilion in the foreground with grey stone columns on carved stone bases and red painted beams, red-lacquered hall behind with pierced lattice frieze and pantile roof, inscribed stone pillar at left, bonsai in ceramic pots. Same pavilion column/base type as the confirmed Tran Ba Dinh shot 4318705108.
Close-up of a pierced openwork timber frieze with green-painted foliage carving beneath a whitewashed ridge and above red pantiles - the same frieze seen in 4317079866 and 4317962337.

Interior altar bay: red and gilt seated deity statues in gold-lacquered niches, red roses, red columns, and a large bronze crane (hac) standing on a turtle in the foreground - the crane pair described in the Ngoc Son bai duong. Inside the confirmed upload run.

Life-size lacquered red horse with white harness inside a gold-and-red temple hall, yellow ceremonial parasol overhead. Same hall as 4318698192, which is one frame from the confirmed Tran Ba Dinh photo 4318705108.
Underside of a yellow ceremonial parasol embroidered with dragons, hung from a red-rafter temple ceiling - the same parasol visible in 4317963777.

Very large banyan with a dense curtain of aerial roots over a stone-paved temple courtyard, a spreading frangipani in front, stone benches, incense smoke from an urn at left. Matches the ancient banyan at the Ngoc Son gate and sits inside the confirmed upload run.

Gilded openwork ceremonial tablet reading 靜肅 (Tinh Tuc, 'be quiet and solemn') hanging from a red-rafter, gold-battened temple roof; the red horse of 4317963777 is visible behind it. Consecutive upload id with the confirmed Tran Ba Dinh photo 4318705108.

Shot through a red temple doorway onto the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion: square grey columns, pierced roof frieze, flagstone paving, a bronze incense urn with dragon handles, and Hoan Kiem Lake water and far shore visible straight through the open pavilion.
Close-up of yellow and red incense sticks planted in ash in a burner in front of red-lacquered doors. No text, no landmark, no wider view.
Turquoise-glazed ceramic guardian lion on a dark wooden stand beside blue-and-white porcelain jars - an antique/souvenir display. No signage or architecture visible.

photos.place: The Huc Bridge, Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Looking along the deck of a red timber bridge: transverse plank decking, vermilion lattice balustrades on both sides, people walking towards a tree-shaded far end - Cau The Huc.
Close selfie of three people with backlit green foliage above. No location cue whatsoever.

photos.place: The Huc Bridge, Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Red timber bridge on red piles hung with a line of festival flags, crossing to a wooded island; lake water in the foreground, a concrete lakeside promenade with pedestrians along the left bank.

Whitewashed gate walls faced with glazed ceramic relief panels (white cranes and pine on a sky-blue ground), balustrade with square red-and-white pierced tiles, patterned cement floor tiles - the decorated gate screens of Ngoc Son, matching 9889297583.
The Nghi Mon gate pillars with the giant red 福 character, couplets 王泮斯 and 立人標... , seated stone animals on the pillar tops - same gate as 4316224355.
The Dac Nguyet Lau gate (grey pillars, tiled roof, red doorway, Han couplet boards) at left and the red The Huc bridge with festival flags at right, over Hoan Kiem Lake water.

Yellow interpretive board legible in three languages: 'DEN NGOC SON / NGOC'SON TEMPLE / TEMPLE NGOC SON (TEMPLE DE LA MONTAGNE DE JADE)', standing next to the grey gate pillar bearing the red 祿 character and 山仰止.

photos.place: The Huc Bridge, Hoan Kiem Lake, Hanoi
photos.evidence: The red The Huc bridge hung with coloured festival flags, seen low across the lake surface with jacaranda-like foliage overhanging the frame.

Paved lakeside walkway with a white balustrade of square pierced tiles running towards the grey Ngoc Son gate arch (Han plaque visible on it), lake water and bathers/onlookers to the left, tourists entering the gate.

The Long Mon gate: 龍門 plaque above, large glazed reliefs of an orange dragon and a white tiger in clouds, and the legible vertical inscription 硯臺筆塔大塊文章 ('ink-slab platform, pen tower') - the Ngoc Son gate that refers to its own Thap But and Dai Nghien.
